newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Fijians test Kronfeld-led S.Island team.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Fijians test Kronfeld-led S.Island team.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, May 28 - All Black test flanker Josh Kronfeld always felt his South Island Invitation side would beat the touring Fijian rugby team on a heavy Victoria Square yesterday, NZPA reports.
Kronfeld captained his side, which included six North Islanders, to a 31-24 win, which ruined Fiji's hopes of an unbeaten tour.

The Fijians want to beat the All Blacks in their one-off test at Albany on June 14 and are also determined to win their other games against Mid-South Canterbury, the Central Vikings, Wanganui and Counties-Manukau.
Fiji coach Brad Johnstone said their aspirations for the tour were to achieve the impossible: beating the All Blacks.
His side rattled in three early tries in their tour opener yesterday and looked as though they might upset Gordon Hunter's collection of promising players.
But Kronfeld, who replaced the injured Todd Blackadder as captain, said he never had any doubts the Fijians would succumb.
"Even though they scored those three tries, I always felt there were chinks in their armour going up the middle with our forwards," Kronfeld said.
"You could feel it, but it was a matter of us trying to get it together. Every time we went wide or through the midfield they cut us to bits.
"Because of the heaviness of the ground, it was hard to get the forwards over to the wide balls."
Coach Hunter got a message to the players to keep the play in close and the forwards put in some superb drives which had the Fijians on the back foot in the final stages.
Fiji led 19-16 at the break but the invitation players ground them down in the second half.
On his 21st birthday, Fero Lasagavibau scored all four of Fiji's tries -- or a point for every pub in the main street of Westport.
Durable second five-eighths Mark Mayerhofler, in the first half, halfback Aaron Flynn and revitalised prop Con Barrell scored for the Invitation side.
Kronfeld said he felt fine after the game, despite taking a solid knock to the same shoulder that kept him out of most of the Super 12 series.
"I caught the nerve and my shoulder went dead for a while. Maybe it needed a rest. But it feels all right now. It was one of those things and I was able to work it clear, so that's good.
"I was not happy with my own game, but I was proud of my players by the way they came back to take a win."
Kronfeld said it took the invitation side much of the game for the new combination to gel and if they had got some of their lineout throws on the button, they could have been more convincing.
"I felt our players showed a lot of courage. We reorganised ourselves, adjusted our strategy and it was a good victory in the end.
"It may not have looked great, but that paddock was just so heavy. It makes you realise what the horses must feel like when they run on a heavy track.
"My boots felt like 200 tonne and when I was trying to support those backs, it was almost impossible," said Kronfeld.
All Blacks coach John Hart said he was satisfied with the efforts of Kronfeld and fellow test contenders Glen Osborne, Mayerhofler, Scott McLeod and Barrell.

Fiji's next game is against Mid-South Canterbury at Timaru on Friday night and Kronfeld predicted the tourists would be a force to be reckoned with in that match and for the rest of the tour if they could improve their set-phase play.
"By the time the test comes around they will be a much better side. They feed well off mistakes so you can't give them an inch," he said.

Johnstone has yet to sort out Fiji's top line-up to take on the All Blacks in their first test this year, but one thing for certain is that big Wellington prop Bill Cavubati will be one of the first selected.
